title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: In tubular Ln36M12 water-oxidation clusters, both a variable-valence lanthanide and multivalent cobalt are important: Eu36Co12 is the most active member, while isostructural Ni clusters are much less active or inactive.
explanation: Under weakly acidic conditions Eu36Co12 outperformed the Gd and Dy cobalt analogues. Eu36Ni12 retained only 24% of the Eu36Co12 activity, and Gd36Ni12 and Dy36Ni12 were essentially inactive. DPV and pH-dependent CV were used to propose cooperative Eu/Co participation in O–O bond formation.
scope: High-nuclearity Ln36Co12 and Ln36Ni12 clusters (Ln = Eu, Gd, Dy) for electrocatalytic water oxidation.
conditions: 0.5 M NaAc/AcOH, pH 5.8, glassy-carbon electrode; Eu36Co12 TON 35, TOF 1.5 s−1, overpotential 0.7 V.
caveats: The detailed O–O mechanism is inferred from voltammetry rather than direct intermediate isolation.
